item.title: Admin Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
I know it's common knowledge that the user whose comment I am replying to was eventually called out

You mean, further down in this thread? Yoric very nearly caught a ban for this post. Nobody "let it slide" even in 2009.

A warning or something, or even an essay concerning how the admins used to be allowed to behave, would in my opinion would be beneficial to new and old users alike.

This is a solution in search of a problem. Soapboxing on an eleven year old thread is nonproductive grandstanding. Take an actual proposal to the forums if you want to, but do not do this again.

item.title: Re: god.
item.content:encoded:
I don't see the utility of an essay that probably very few people would read, and, of those who would read, most are the kind of people who read community guideline essays for fun. Similarly, it seems like a poor use of staff time to have them reply to comments from departed users //in an official capacity saying "this was very naughty, do not do it." We already have guidelines in the form of crit policy and general site rules that effectively prohibit behaving like people from the bad old days. People who think that it's still an acceptable way to behave quickly find themselves the holder of a warning, if not ban. I feel like if you want to reinforce a rule, "don't do this or you are going to be kicked off the site" is much more effective than an essay that few people will read, or a few scattered comments.

Then again, I'm no longer staff, so maybe this would be a welcome change.

item.title: Re: god.
item.content:encoded:
Just to make things clear — I didn't mean to warn Yoric or Bright themselves, but rather to warn new users (by potentially editing offending comments by y, b and others) that the kind of bullshit that was allowed to slide in 2009 is by no means allowed to slide today.

People who just get into this website from the satellite communities and greater fandom seem to consider people like Bright paragons of great writing, and may even seek to emulate their behavior and further their shitty jokes (an example: Bright's List). I believe that nipping that sort of thought in the bud right away would be a huge benefit to the wiki as a whole.

item.title: Re: god.
item.content:encoded:
A warning or something, or even an essay concerning how the admins used to be allowed to behave, would in my opinion would be beneficial to new and old users alike.

In what way?

Anyone who uses a version of Yoric or Bright's posts from 2010 as a guide for how to behave will find themselves quickly disabused via warning/banning.

I honestly don't see the benefit of creating an essay or centralized hub for pointing out that people sucked ten years ago strikes me as, at absolute best, completely pointless, and at worst, the kind of creepy and vindictive "looklook, i found the receipts"-posting that preserves people at their worst and most immature.

The idea of giving someone who last posted here four years ago a warning for a post that they made ten years ago is absurd and more than a little comical.

item.title: god.
item.content:encoded:
I know that this is a necropost, but this really needs to be said.

There's got to be more done about how absolutely awful most of the "old guard" of wiki staff are (or were, if you're being optimistic) as people. I had no idea at all about the deeper murk of wiki "history" as a new user, and even in the past year I was mostly blind to how these people used to be allowed to act — it's saddening that some people might not even see these examples of shitty mod behaviour and consider these old mods their wiki role models, and even more troubling that some people might see this behaviour and think that it's ok just because some popular old-guard member of staff acted like this on the regular.

I know it's common knowledge that the user whose comment I am replying to was eventually called out, at least among people who know quite a bit about wiki "history," but the fact that it took so long for me to find such examples of blatant scummery makes me wonder if leaving the relevant info concerning these people where some people might find it eventually is really enough. A warning or something, or even an essay concerning how the admins used to be allowed to behave, would in my opinion would be beneficial to new and old users alike.

There is a chance that I'm making mountains out of molehills and getting riled up over something that isn't too bad, but that's just my two cents. Do with it what you will.

item.title: Could be added to Scp 173
item.content:encoded:
Due to its size and destructive nature, containment procedures have been changed to include more secure and efficient containment procedures. After a breach of containment, all personnel involved are restrained and immediately considered missing in action.

If SCP-173 is on surveillance it will immediately target the nearest surveillance camera. If possible, equipment must be recovered before being targeted. If a surveillance camera is not accessible for anything other than maintenance, the item may not target it.
